title: Best AI Tricks To Gain Advantage
description:
Why should you never trust ChatGPT?

Most people get a single answer from AI and immediately accept it as the final result.

AI strategist Geoff Woods warns that this is a fatal mistake.

His hack forces the machine to turn on itself, exposing every hidden bias and crack in your foundation.

Stop settling for lazy drafts.

There are two ways to use AI 

Creativity- ask for ideas and base it as much factual data as possible
Project Management- an automated agent to gather data and flow of operations without your supervision

top_comments.author: @badadviceforfree
top_comments.text: My hacks: tell it to ask you the questions it would be useful to know about you to inform it's future interactions (values etc). Tell it how to speak to you (succinct, warm, friendly but not too agreeable), tell it the quality of results you want, tell it to fact check you, tell it not to dumb things down (assume I'm intelligent), tell it not to compliment you unless there's something genuinely stand out that it would be useful to know, but no pointless fluffing you up (assume I have a healthy self esteem and don't need validation) and also I love asking for any neuroscience research discoveries that are relevant to what we are doing. I find it excels at being a researcher, marketing and media assistant, legal and technical assistants, psychology theory. It is mediocre at: writing scripts, education content (absence of classroom experience makes a huge difference). Biggest take home: what you know on a subject will dictate how you approach the AI, be aware if you are an amateur on something you won't be able to spot the medicrity or flaws and you can assume there is a good chance it's sub par, generic, and dumbed down, for the maximum audience. You can still guide it to assess its own work and improve it. Ask it to  critique its own work for a specific audience or publication. Tell it to avoid cliches. And use manners. Don't let using technology be the thing that makes you comfortable with lower standards.
